subject: Post-call: Cumulus Systems — inference topology & SLOs
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@cumulussys.com>, Marco Ruiz <m.ruiz@cumulussys.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap + SLO / topology attachments

Hi Ellen / Marco —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap from my side and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. I’ve attached a draft SLO matrix and a rough deployment topology diagram (see attachments).

Key pain points you called out:
- Current response variability during morning batch jobs (peak bursts) causing tail latency spikes and customer-reported timeouts.
- High per-request cost on current CPU-based inference; need a predictable unit cost for forecasting.
- Regulatory/audit concerns: need detailed request logs, retention policy, and KMS integration.

Stated goals / success metrics:
- p95 generation latency target: <= 250 ms (targeting 200 ms if feasible) for the primary chat endpoint.
- Sustained throughput: ~800 QPS during normal hours; burst capacity to handle ~1,800 req/min for short windows.
- Model quality: match current baseline (in-house tuned LLM) with plan to evaluate 13B/7B candidate variants.
- Security: SOC2 evidence and VPC/private deployment, encryption in transit + at rest.

Technical highlights we discussed:
- Recommendation: dedicated GPU pool in us-west-2 for primary traffic + automatic overflow to hosted capacity during spikes.
- KV / prefix caching to reduce repeat token work for sessioned chat.
- Two-tier model strategy: high-quality 13B for mission-critical routes, quantized 7B as fallback for cost-sensitive paths.
- Observability: per-request token-level latency and cost breakdowns exposed in Console; we can export logs to your SIEM.

Attachments included: cumulus-systems-slo-matrix.xlsx (draft), deployment-topology-diagram.png

Immediate next steps (proposed):
1) Share non-prod access instructions — I’ll send a short screencast to get your infra team connected to our sandbox. (Attachment: rdw-nonprod-access-screencast.mp4)
2) Technical deep-dive (capacity mapping + quantization options) — propose Tue 12/16 or Wed 12/17, 10:00–11:30 PT.
3) We’ll run a small benchmark against a 7B quantized variant in non-prod to validate p95 and throughput assumptions.

Could you confirm: preferred deep-dive time, AWS account for non-prod access (we need an IAM role), and procurement contact for contracting questions?

Thanks — looking forward to the next steps.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0124

From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@cumulussys.com>

Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 18:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + SLO / topology attachments

Thanks Jasmine — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side: we run most inference today on EC2 (us-west-2) with an autoscaling CPU fleet; pushing to GPU is the main change we’re evaluating to hit the latency goals.

Priority clarifications:
- Our immediate internal target is p95 <= 200 ms for short-form generation (we appreciate the 250 ms note as a conservative target).
- Burst windows are typically 5–7 minutes during morning syncs and at EOD; that’s when we see the biggest failures.

Questions for the deep-dive:
1) Which quantization formats do you support out-of-the-box (int8, int4)? Any recommended fallbacks that keep quality stable?
2) Can we get an SOC2 artifact or an overview of how audit logs are retained and delivered?

Procurement is cc’d here (procurement@cumulussys.com) — they’ll start the paperwork once we confirm a topology and cost estimate.

—Ellen
Ellen Park
Head of ML Systems | Cumulus Systems
ellen.park@cumulussys.com

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + SLO / topology attachments — proposed topology and test plan

Ellen — thanks for the quick reply and for looping procurement. A few items to accelerate the deep-dive:

Short pre-read (bulleted):
- Quantization: we support both dynamic int8 and an experimental int4 path for selected 7B variants. For production we generally recommend int8 for 7B and mixed-int8/mixed-f16 for 13B to preserve quality. We’ll bring quality delta numbers to the call.
- Suggested topology (draft):
  * Primary: Redwood Dedicated pool in us-west-2 (pinned GPU nodes) serving sessioned chat endpoints.
  * KV/prefix cache layer colocated with the pool to reduce repeated token compute.
  * Fallback route: smaller quantized model in the hosted fleet with automatic routing for capacity overflow or degraded nodes.
  * Observability: per-route dashboards + exportable audit logs to your S3/SIEM.
- Bench plan: we’ll run a 30-minute sustained workload at expected p95 targets and a separate 10-minute burst sim to validate autoscale and routing behavior.

Practical asks for the call:
1) IAM role or account/email we can add to our sandbox for non-prod benchmarking.
2) Example traffic profile: average tokens per request, median/90/99 token counts, and concurrency distribution (if you’ve got it).
3) Any regulatory constraints beyond SOC2 (e.g., data residency rules).

I’m attaching the access screencast (rdw-nonprod-access-screencast.mp4) — it’s a 4-minute walkthrough for your infra team. If the team can provision the role by Monday we’ll run a smoke benchmark before the deep-dive.

Rishi — can you validate the initial GPU sizing below and add any cost/ops notes before the deep-dive?

Thanks,
Jasmine

Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + SLO / topology attachments — sizing notes

Quick internal sizing notes — posting here so Jasmine / Sean have visibility ahead of the deep-dive.

Assumptions from the call: p95 target 200–250 ms, sustained ~800 QPS, short bursts up to ~30 QPS (1,800 req/min), avg tokens/request ~120 (need confirmation).

Initial recommendation (sustained + burst):
- Start: 4 x A100-80GB equivalent (pinned) to handle baseline throughput with KV cache enabled. Expect ~800 QPS sustained with optimized batching.
- Autoscale/commit: policy to scale to 10–12 GPU nodes for bursts (or overflow to hosted capacity).
- Model strategy: 13B (mixed-fp16 + optimized kernels) as primary for highest quality; 7B int8 quantized as fallback to keep unit cost low on non-critical routes.

Operational notes:
- We’ll need to validate memory footprint with your typical context window; large chat histories may push KV storage needs.
- Prefix caching will dramatically reduce steady-state compute if users frequently repeat prompts.
- If token length average is >200, recommend increasing baseline to 6 GPUs.

Open items to bring to the deep-dive:
- Concrete tokens distribution (median / p95 / p99)
- Example request payload size and concurrency spikes during your reported windows
- Any throughput caps in your network or WAF that could shape architecture

I’ll prepare a short cost/ops slide for the call showing a 3-month commitment vs on-demand estimate.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Lead Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
